query: MCX-MCX产品的主要使用对象？
gold_answer: 警察、轨交、应急
agent_answer:
MCX产品的主要使用对象分为两类：

**1. 公共安全领域用户（核心对象）**

对通信可靠性和可用性要求极高的公共安全场合，包括：
- 公安
- 消防
- 医疗急救
- 应急救援

**2. 对高可靠、高优先级通信有需求的企业用户**

- 大型赛事安保
- 重大事件保障
- 大型能源、矿场、机场、轨道交通、汽车制造等生产企业

**说明**：MCSTARS产品基于核心网的MC专用承载和QPP策略，为关键任务的执行提供高优先级、高可靠、高可用的保证，即上述用户都是围绕“关键任务通信”这一核心定位展开的。

> 来源：MCX-资料 / 《MCSTARS关键任务通信系统产品V1.1.1》产品介绍（产品定位章节）

retrieved_chunks.content:
产品定位
MCSTARS产品基于核心网网络的MC专用承载和QPP策略，为关键任务的执行提供了高优先级、高可靠、高可用的保证，守护公共安全生命线，适用于公安、消防、医疗急救及应急救援等对通信可靠性和可用性要求极高的公共安全场合。产品突出的特性也适用于对通信可靠性、可用性及高优先级要求较高的大型赛事安保、重大事件保障、大型能源、矿场、机场、轨道交通、汽车制造等生产企业。
适用场景
MCX产品
# MCX产品特点
- 高清语音、高清视频、多媒体数据(图片、文件等)
- 聚合统一客户端、支持多路音频、视频并发
- 高效、协作调度台，基于浏览器，跨系统
- 高清视频、多媒体数据等详细态势感知，做出正确决策和指令下达
丰富的集群业务
- 独立APN访问网络，隔离其它系统、数据和用户
- 三重用户准入控制，防止非法用户访问系统
- 端到端信令、媒体及应用层全方位加密
- 设备、客户端及用户统一管理
- 多租户隔离、数据加密、数据审计、备份与恢复
业务和数据安全性
- 支持普通固定及临时群组管理，满足日常调度
- 支持Adhoc临时群组业务，任务结束即解散，应对突发事件和转向活动
- 支持高精度定位，位置控制人员加入或退出群组业务，实现智能动态调度管理
- 优先级管理，区分任务优先级，调度优先级等，强化分级调度管理
灵活调度、强化管理
- 微服务架构、组件化产品
- 独立部署、快速、持续交付，降低影响范围
- 更高可用性、故障隔离、降低服务风险
- 资源高效利用、精准扩容、负载均衡策略灵活

### 1. Introduction Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) is a 3GPP standardized voice service for mobile radio systems which ensures that LTE and 5G systems support mission-critical communications. The global mission-critical communication market was valued at approximately US$17.03 billion in 2022 and is projected to reach US$27.88 billion by 2028, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8.6% during the forecast period as per the Insight Partners. This growth is driven by the increasing adoption of mission-critical communication systems across various sectors, including public safety, transportation, energy, utilities, and mining. Several regions have initiated nationwide rollouts of mission-critical LTE or 5G networks, leading to significant investments in this sector. Notably, countries such as the United States, South Korea, Finland, France, and various nations in the Middle East and Asia have been at the forefront of these developments, as per GlobeNewswire. Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) was the first of several Mission Critical features standardized by 3GPP in Release-13. Mission Critical Video and Mission Critical Data standardization started with Release-14. With the standardization of MCX (Mission-Critical PTT, Video & Data) and other critical communications features by 3GPP, LTE and 5G NR networks are increasingly gaining recognition as an all-inclusive communications platform for public safety, rail, utilities and other critical communications sectors. Preparations for the 9th ETSI MCX Plugtests event started in October 2024 with the registrations of vendors and observers. During bi-weekly conference calls from October 2024 to February 2025 the setup of the tests, the test specification and organizational discussions were agreed between the participants. Before the main event, the vendors integrated with the test network and remote pre-testing of their implementations via VPN tunnels, which connected their labs to a central exchange hub. All the information required to organise and manage the 9th MCX Plugtests event was compiled and shared with participants in a dedicated private WIKI which was put in place by ETSI. All participants were provided with credentials that allowed them to access and update their details. All the information presented in this document has been extracted from the 9th MCX Plugtests event wiki: https://wiki.plugtests.net/9th-MCX-Plugtests/ (login required). Clause 4 describes the management of the Plugtests event. The following equipment was tested – please see also clause 5: MCX Application Servers (MCX AS) MCX Clients • Evolved Node B (eNB)

Several regions have initiated nationwide rollouts of mission-critical LTE or 5G networks, leading to significant investments in this sector. Notably, countries such as the United States, South Korea, Finland, France, the United Kingdom, Norway, Sweden and various nations in the Middle East and Asia have been at the forefront of these developments. The transition is further accelerated by nationwide LTE/5G build-outs enabling network slicing, edge analytics, and new tools for situational awareness.
Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) was the first of several Mission Critical features standardized by 3GPP in Release-13. Mission Critical Video and Mission Critical Data standardization started with Release-14. With the standardization of MCX (Mission-Critical PTT, Video & Data) and other critical communications features by 3GPP, LTE and 5G NR networks are increasingly gaining recognition as an all-inclusive communications platform for public safety, rail, utilities and other critical communications sectors.
Preparations for the 10th ETSI MCX Plugtests event started in December 2025 with the registrations of vendors and observers in January and February 2026. During bi-weekly conference calls from January 2026 to May 2026, the setup of the tests, the test specification and organisational discussions were agreed between the participants. Before the main event, the vendors integrated with the test network and conducted remote pre-testing of their implementations via VPN tunnels, which connected their labs to a central exchange hub at ETSI.
The VPN integration phase ran from 23rd March to 10th April 2026, followed by integration with 4G and 5G test networks from 13th April to 30th April 2026, and a one-week pre-testing phase from 4th to 8th May 2026. The main face-to-face interoperability testing event took place from 18th to 22nd May 2026 at the ETSI premises in Sophia Antipolis, France.
All the information required to organise and manage the 10th MCX Plugtests event was compiled and shared with participants in a dedicated private WIKI which was put in place by ETSI. All participants were provided with credentials that allowed them to access and update their details. All the information presented in this document has been extracted from the 10th MCX Plugtests event wiki (login required).

In this Plugtests, multiple Application Servers and Clients were evaluated in dedicated test streams (Stream A & B). Stream A was available for vendors to evaluate their equipment for end-to-end interoperability testing over 4G networks (Bands 38/40), and Stream B for testing over 5G networks (Band 78). In this Plugtests it was required to test each Application Server with at least 2 different Client implementations.
The Interworking Function (IWF) with LMR systems (TETRA) was evaluated in a dedicated IWF test stream (Stream C). Stream D was available for vendors to evaluate their equipment in interconnected MCX systems (Inter-MCX, server-to-server communication). eMBMS multicast functionality was tested in a dedicated test stream (Stream E), which was available for multicast service centre, gateway and MCX server/client vendors to test multicast implementations.

## Executive Summary
The capabilities of Mission Critical Push to Talk (MCPTT), Mission Critical Data (MCData) and Mission Critical Video (MCVideo) – together abbreviated as MCX services – were tested during the tenth MCX Plugtests from 18 May to 22 May 2026 at the ETSI premises in Sophia Antipolis, France using 4G and 5G test networks.
The 10th ETSI MCX Plugtests have concluded with a success rate of 92% of the executed tests in the validation of 3GPP mission critical services vendor interoperability. More than 240 delegates participated during the 10th MCX Plugtests event on-site in Sophia Antipolis and off-site from their labs, making it the largest MCX Plugtests to date.
These tests are essential to ensuring seamless access to mission-critical services over 4G and 5G networks across different vendor products and implementations.
The MCX ETSI Plugtests series is the first independent testing of public safety and other mission critical services over 4G/LTE and 5G networks. The Interworking Function (IWF) to LMR (narrowband Land Mobile Radio networks) systems like TETRA, Interconnection (Inter-MCX) between MCX servers, eMBMS (multicast), conformance test tools and performance testing tools were particularly tested in these 10th MCX Plugtests. The preparations for the tenth Plugtests started with VPN integration from 23rd March to 10th April 2026, followed by integration with 4G and 5G test networks from 13th April to 30th April 2026, a one-week pre-testing phase from 4th to 8th May 2026, and were finalized with one week of face-to-face end-to-end interoperability testing with 4G and 5G test networks at ETSI in Sophia Antipolis.

MCSTARS 产品是基于3GPP 标准协议（Rel-18），研发推出的新一代关键任务通信系统。系统包含关键任务MCPTT、MCVideo及MCData三个标准业务子系统，提供语音、视频及数据等多媒体集群业务。系统满足关键任务对网络高可靠性、高质量及安全的需求，对跨系统、跨地区和国家互联互通的需求，可实现大规模组网。遵循标准协议，持续演进，具备灵活的业务扩展和接入能力。

### 1.2 公司简介
善理通益创立于2010年，专注通信指挥调度领域，是创新型解决方案提供商与运营服务商，全力推动集群通信技术及行业方案发展。公司以深圳为核心，在石家庄、西安、青岛设有研发与客户支撑点，海外多国设办事处助力全球业务拓展。
旗下POCSTARS是面向全球的产品品牌，提供多款面向不同市场的解决方案：POCSTARS-MNO专为运营商设计，POCSTARS-PRO针对中小企业市场，POCSTARS-UC面向行业客户，以及遵循3GPP MCX标准的MCSTARS产品。秉持“链接新边界”理念，集成对讲机终端、宽窄带通信集群网络、新一代指挥调度系统、公网电话、IOT设备、视频监控、多模定位技术、3D GIS以及AI计算机视觉等多种技术，打造功能强大的综合指挥调度平台，提供信息汇聚、辅助决策等服务，保障通讯安全可靠，提升协作效率。
自2018年起，善理通益与中国移动合作打造“和对讲”平台，为超300万客户、超10万家企业提供便捷“一键对讲”服务，严格遵循移动高标准，2024年荣获“最佳合作伙伴”称号。
作为技术驱动型企业，善理通益每年投入数千万元研发，已获50多项核心专利，依托3G至5G技术积累成果丰硕。行业解决方案覆盖公共安全、危化能源、轨道交通、园区安保、医疗等多领域，服务客户1000万+，1000+合作伙伴，产品与服务广受赞誉。
随着国际化战略的稳步推进，截至2025年，POCSTARS在海外设十余个通讯云节点，支持二十多种语言，为数百万用户提供高可靠服务与本土化界面，多国设分支机构开拓市场。善理通益始终坚持以先进技术、优质产品，聚焦细分需求，为客户提供高性价比通信产品与行业方案，同时与运营商、集成商、终端厂商共同开拓全球市场，携手伙伴构建多赢商业生态。

#### 2.2.3 标准演进
MCX系统以3GPP Rel-18标准为基础设计开发，全球统一标准，产品根据标准的持续演进迭代更新产品，兼容后续版本标准，确保协议一致性，支持未来网络。
善理通益致力于推动3GPP MCX标准的国产化，加入了CCSA，作为CCSA TC5工作组成员，参与4G/5G核心网、应急工作组标准工作，参与的MCX国产化行业标准《5G任务服务（MCX）通信系统总体技术要求》已于2026年1月完成立项。
![image_1786159015846313.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159015848529_image_1786159015846313.png)
图 -4 CCSA会员证书
并于2025年10月在2025世界物联网博览会·5G-A×AI赋能行业应用创新论坛上联合中国移动研究院发布了《面向关键任务的群组通信（MCX）技术白皮书》。
![image_1786159015853157.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159015855314_image_1786159015853157.png)
![image_1786159015858946.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159015861007_image_1786159015858946.png)
图 -5 《面向关键任务的群组通信（MCX）技术白皮书》
#### 2.2.4 灵活部署
MCX系统支持灵活的组网方式，支持不依赖核心网的OTT模式，作为应用平台纯IP接入；支持基于运营商网络部署，部署在运营商的4G/5G网络中，利用现有的移动网络基础设施提供关键任务通信服务，充分利用运营商的网络覆盖和资源，快速实现大范围的通信能力；还支持专网部署和宽窄带融合部署，灵活的部署方式使得MCX系统能够适应不同的应用场景和需求，无论是公共安全、交通、能源还是其他关键任务领域，都能提供可靠的通信解决方案。

query: MCX-MCX中语音对讲保障的QCI？
gold_answer: 5QI Value：65
agent_answer:
MCX 中语音对讲（MCPTT）业务使用的保障 QCI 为 **65**（4G 网络中 QCI=65，5G 网络中对应 5QI=65），属于 GBR 资源类型。

具体 QoS 参数如下：

| 网络 | 标识 | 资源类型 | 优先级 | 时延 | 丢包率 | 典型应用 |
|------|------|---------|--------|-------|--------|---------|
| 4G | QCI=65 | GBR | 0.7 | 75 ms | 10⁻² | 关键任务用户面一键通语音（如 MCPTT） |
| 5G | 5QI=65 | GBR | 7 | 75 ms | 10⁻² | 关键任务用户面一键通语音（如 MCPTT） |

补充说明：

1. **相对普通语音的优势**：与通用语音业务 QCI=1（优先级 2，时延 100 ms）相比，MCX 语音 MCPTT 的 QCI=65 优先级更高（0.7），时延更低（75 ms），保证 MCX 语音业务在核心网获得优先调度。
2. **MCX 全套专用标识**：3GPP 标准为 MCX 定义了专用承载标识——语音 65、视频 67、信令 69、数据 70；语音（65）和视频（67）为 GBR 类型，预留空口和网络资源，任何时候保证资源可用。
3. **适用条件**：上述 QoS 保障依赖 4G/5G 网络的 QCI/5QI 策略配置；若采用 OTT 纯 IP 接入方式部署，则不具备该 QoS 保障机制。

来源：
- 《MCSTARS产品白皮书V1.1.1.docx》（知识库：MCX-资料）
- 《MCX基于5GC专用承载与默认承载的差异说明 V1.0.docx》（知识库：补充）

#### 2.4.2 基于核心网
在4G/5G网络中，QoS定义了不同数据流的传输优先级、资源分配及性能保障机制，确保各类业务获得符合其需求的承载。QCI是QoS的分类标识（5G网络中叫5QI），以数字标识一组预定义的QoS特性（如：优先级、资源类型、允许的最大时延、允许的最大丢包率等），网络设备（如基站、核心网）根据QCI快速匹配预定义的QoS规则，应用相应的资源分配策略。下面两个表格分别是3GPP标准提供的4G网络中标准QCI分类和5G网络中的5QI分类，可以保证QCI值在不同厂商设备间通用，确保跨网络QoS一致性。

#### 2.4.3 微服务架构
![image_1786159015899151.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159015900996_image_1786159015899151.png)

MCX系统基于微服务化架构，平台组件间耦合性降至最低，支持多实例集群化部署。
产品支持容器化部署，极大提升开发、部署与运维效率。
部署操作支持一键部署脚本。
系统采用无状态服务设计理念，这种设计方式极大地提升了单台节点的并发处理能力。由于无状态服务不需要在服务器端保存客户端的会话状态信息，服务器可以更高效地处理多个客户端的请求，减少了服务器的处理负担。同时，这种设计降低了服务器的成本，无论是硬件成本还是运营成本都得到了有效控制，为系统的大规模部署和长期运行提供了经济、高效的解决方案。

![image_1786159011104428.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159011106406_image_1786159011104428.png)

The MCX system adopts a fully microservice-based architecture, this architecture minimizes coupling between platform components. and it supports multi-instance clustered deployment.
The MCX system supports containerized deployment, which significantly improves development, deployment, and operational efficiency.
The deployment operation supports a one-click deployment script.
The system adopts a stateless service design concept. This design approach greatly enhances the concurrent processing capability of a single node. Since stateless services do not require the server to save client session state information, the server can more efficiently handle requests from multiple clients, reducing the server's processing burden. Meanwhile, this design reduces server costs, effectively controlling both hardware and operational costs, and provides an economical and efficient solution for the large-scale deployment and long-term operation of the system.
#### 2.4.4 Data Segregation
**Multi-tenant Architecture**
The system adopts a multi-tenant architecture, basic data and business data are stored in isolated environments for each tenant,where each tenant (user) can have an independent data storage space.

## 应用服务器 由 MC 服务器、MC 用户数据库和 MC 网关服务器构成。通过统一的用户数据管理（MC 用户数据库）以及一组通用的服务功能（CSC）为用户提供语音（MCPTT）、视频（MCVideo）、数据（MCData）等多媒体应用，依托 MC 网关服务器实现对 MC 网络与不同信任域 MC 网络之间的互连，同时提供拓扑隐藏，提高网络安全性。 #### 2.2.2 “4” 大关键能力 ##### 2.2.2.1 优先保障 在网络拥塞或紧急场景下，正常数据传输易出现延迟、丢包问题，而关键任务集群数据包一般携带应急调度指令、实时业务协作等关键信息，传递受阻会直接导致应急响应滞后、核心业务中断，严重情况下会危及生命或使重要资产处于危险中。 针对上述痛点需求，MCX 网络需要具备完善的 QPP（QCI + Priority + Pre-emption）保障机制、支持在专用网络切片承载业务，通过动态调整端到端参数、配置高抢占能力、通过专用网络切片承载建立 MCX 业务，从而确保在网络拥塞或紧急情况下能够优先传递集群数据包。
图 4 5G QoS 流建立
### 1. 端到端参数动态调整 为实现端到端参数动态调整，网络侧需能够根据业务需求动态调整 QoS 参数，包括 QCI 和 Priority 接入优先级。5G 网络可以通过策略控制功能（PCF）触发策略更改、设置 PCC 规则，触发 5G QoS 流的创建或修改。 ### 2. 配置高抢占能力 抢占能力是确保 MCX 网络在拥塞期间能够拒绝非特权用户的访问 / 资源请求，同时允许新的 MC 用户抢占非特权用户的网络资源，确保 MC 用户可以始终访问蜂窝网络资源，防止 QoS Flow 级别的拥塞。

# MCX System Architecture
The MCX mission-critical communication system is built on 4G/5G core network and IMS architecture, deeply integrated with both to deliver broadband trunked voice, video and data services. It supports mission-critical dedicated bearer, off-network/disconnected communication, multicast/broadcast and other characteristic services, is compatible with non-standard command & dispatch services, and converges narrowband trunked services such as Tetra, DMR and PDT.
MCX and 4G LTE Network Architecture
MCX services hold the highest priority in the core network
- Highest-priority QoS Guarantee (Low Latency, High Reliability)
- Highest-priority Service in the Core Network
- Resource Preemption (Preempting Lower-priority Resources)

## 1 Introduction Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) is a 3GPP standardized voice service for mobile radio systems which ensures that LTE (and 5G) systems support mission-critical communications. The Global Mission-Critical Communication Market was valued at USD 17.03 billion in 2022 and is estimated to reach USD 27.87 billion by 2028 growing at a CAGR of 8.6% during the forecast period 2022–2028, according to the market research. The global train control and management systems market is expected to grow from $3.73 billion in 2022 to $3.99 billion in 2023 at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 7.2%. The nationwide rollouts in the European countries are expected to trigger significant large-scale investments in mission-critical 5G. Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) was the first of a number of Mission Critical features which was standardized by 3GPP in Release-13. Mission Critical Video and Mission Critical Data were standardized in Release-14. With the standardization of MCX (Mission-Critical PTT, Video & Data), FRMCS, and other critical communications features by 3GPP, ETSI and UIC, 5G networks are increasingly gaining recognition as an all-inclusive communication platform for public safety, railways, utilities, maritime and other critical communications sectors.

### 1. Introduction Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) is a 3GPP standardized voice service for mobile radio systems which ensures that LTE and 5G systems support mission-critical communications. The global mission-critical communication market was valued at approximately US$17.03 billion in 2022 and is projected to reach US$27.88 billion by 2028, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8.6% during the forecast period as per the Insight Partners. This growth is driven by the increasing adoption of mission-critical communication systems across various sectors, including public safety, transportation, energy, utilities, and mining. Several regions have initiated nationwide rollouts of mission-critical LTE or 5G networks, leading to significant investments in this sector. Notably, countries such as the United States, South Korea, Finland, France, and various nations in the Middle East and Asia have been at the forefront of these developments, as per GlobeNewswire. Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) was the first of several Mission Critical features standardized by 3GPP in Release-13. Mission Critical Video and Mission Critical Data standardization started with Release-14. With the standardization of MCX (Mission-Critical PTT, Video & Data) and other critical communications features by 3GPP, LTE and 5G NR networks are increasingly gaining recognition as an all-inclusive communications platform for public safety, rail, utilities and other critical communications sectors. Preparations for the 9th ETSI MCX Plugtests event started in October 2024 with the registrations of vendors and observers. During bi-weekly conference calls from October 2024 to February 2025 the setup of the tests, the test specification and organizational discussions were agreed between the participants. Before the main event, the vendors integrated with the test network and remote pre-testing of their implementations via VPN tunnels, which connected their labs to a central exchange hub. All the information required to organise and manage the 9th MCX Plugtests event was compiled and shared with participants in a dedicated private WIKI which was put in place by ETSI. All participants were provided with credentials that allowed them to access and update their details. All the information presented in this document has been extracted from the 9th MCX Plugtests event wiki: https://wiki.plugtests.net/9th-MCX-Plugtests/ (login required). ## Executive Summary
The capabilities of Mission Critical Push to Talk (MCPTT), Mission Critical Data (MCData) and Mission Critical Video (MCVideo) – together abbreviated as MCX services – were tested during the ninth MCX Plugtests from 24 $ ^{th} $ February to 28 $ ^{th} $ February 2025 at the The Center for Infrastructure Renewal (CIR) part of Texas A&M University System (TAMUS) in College Station, Texas, USA using 4G and 5G test networks. 174 test cases were executed between vendors, based on 3GPP Release 18.
The 9th ETSI MCX Plugtests have concluded with a success rate of 83% of the executed tests in the validation of 3GPP mission critical services vendor interoperability. More than 200 delegates participated during the  $ 9^{th} $ MCX Plugtests event on-site in College Station and off-site from their labs.

U_{E} UIC .uns de fer) User Equipment International union of railways (Union Internationale des Chemins de fer) ### 4. Technical and Project Management ### 4.1 Scope The main goal of the ninth MCX Plugtests was testing the interoperability of the MCPTT, MCData and MCVideo ecosystem signalling and media plane at different levels. The Multi-client scenarios, Off-Network, Inter MCX, Multicast and interworking (IWF) with LMR were tested during the event. The basic scenario tested comprised MCX application server(s) - both controlling and participating- and multiple MCX clients deployed over a generic SIP/IMS core, LTE & 5G access network with and without MCX required PCC capabilities with native multicast support (i.e. Release-14 - and higher- eMBMS) and UEs. The following Figure 1 illustrates the basic test infrastructure. Additionally, off-network communications between two UEs using 5G sidelink was evaluated.
### Figure 1. Typical MCPTT/MCData/MCVideo scenario to be considered in the Plugtests In the scope of this Plugtests event, the following high level test objectives were performed. - Connectivity (CONN): Tests covered basic connectivity between functional elements at different levels including Access Network (LTE), IP Network, SIP/IMS and MCPTT/MCData/MCVideo Application level. At LTE level, unicast and more particularly eMBMS multicast connectivity was evaluated. Tests at IP layer targeted pure OTT connectivity regardless the underlying access network. SIP connectivity tests checked proper deployment of MCX AS over the selected SIP Core/IMS so that all SIP messages were successfully delivered from MCX Clients to Participating/Controlling MCPTT Servers and vice versa. In this 9th Plugtests, AS vendors provided their own built-in SIP/IMS cores so that Clients registered into different cores depending on the specific test session. Application level refers to e2e signalling, media, floor controlling (and other involved) protocols in use. Plugtests participants were encouraged to carry on CONN tests over Mission Critical LTE/5G for unicast – or UNI-MC-LTE/5G – and Mission Critical LTE with multicast eMBMS capabilities – so called MULTI-MC-LTE. Additionally, low level configuration-specific details (i.e. MCPTT, MC QCI and eMBMS bearer management) were considered in the PCC and eMBMS specific objectives. MCData and MCVideo fea tures were mostly analysed in test cases associated to the CONN objective while sibling procedures (i.e. registration to different MCPTT/MCData/MCVideo servers) were carried out when needed. - eMBMS (EMBMS): Comprised checking of eMBMS specific signalling both in the MB2-U/C interface and e2e. - Multi IOP: Interoperability testing-oriented complex test cases were added for Multi-client scenarios. - Interworking Function (IWF): MCPTT connectivity test cases were re-used to test interworking with LMR systems (Tetra and P25). - Inter MCX: MCPTT/MCVideo connectivity test cases were used to test interworking between application servers. Off-Network: MCPTT off network test cases were used to test direct mode communication using Sidelink UEs. ### 4.2 Timeline The preparation was run through different phases as described in the Figure 2 below.

MCX采用符合3GPP标准的安全架构和机制，支持端到端加密，能够有效防止数据泄露、篡改和未经授权的访问。且兼容性强，能与其他符合该标准的系统在同样的安全机制下进行互操作。
- 1． **宽窄融合**
PoC作为独立的应用层服务，无法直接与TETRA、PDT、P25等窄带集群系统对接，若客户已有LMR投资，需额外采购专用网关且功能受限，通常仅能支持语音互通，数据和视频无法跨系统流转。
MCX在3GPP标准中明确定义了IWF互操作功能，可实现与LMR系统的标准化对接，帮助客户在保护既有投资的同时平滑向宽带演进。
- 1． **业务框架**
PoC的业务能力以语音对讲为核心，部分厂商扩展了定位、图文消息、视频通话等功能，但均为私有实现，无统一标准保障，视频和数据能力在质量、时延、可靠性方面取决于网络质量，适合简单工作协同场景。
MCX定义了三大标准化服务——MCPTT（关键任务一键通）、MCVideo（关键任务视频）、MCData（关键任务数据），每项服务均有明确的QoS指标、信令流程和优先级机制，可实现语音、视频、数据的一体化融合调度，支撑复杂业务场景。
- 1． **系统演进**
公网PoC：功能迭代依赖厂商自身规划，无统一技术演进路线。
MCX：依托3GPP标准持续迭代，R17已支持卫星接入（NTN），R18引入AI增强，未来可平滑升级至5G-A及6G，是行业未来十年关键通信的统一演进底座。
### 2.3 应用场景
| 场景              | 推荐方案        | 原因                                      |
|-----------------|-------------|-----------------------------------------|
| 警察、消防、急救指挥      | MCX         | 通信失败=生命损失                               |
| 铁路/地铁调度、港口/机场运营 | MCX         | 视频+数据是刚需，网络级保障  3GPP已定义铁路FRMCS标准替代GSM-R |

MCX基于3GPP全球统一标准，不同厂商设备可天然互通，同时通过标准化的IWF（Interworking Function）互操作功能，能够与存量LMR窄带集群系统实现语音、数据、控制信令的双向互通，支持宽窄融合调度，特别适合需要跨部门、跨区域、跨系统协同的复杂指挥场景。
- 1． **产业链**
PoC的产业链成熟度较高，终端侧可利用市面上绝大多数通用对讲机、智能手机、执法仪、平板、三防/车载终端，芯片和模组供应链成熟且成本极低，客户选择面广、更换成本低，这使其能够快速渗透企业市场。
MCX的产业链相对聚焦于专用领域，终端需通过3GPP合规认证，芯片和模组成本较高，但产业链正在随着全球公共安全宽带化建设持续扩展，主流通信芯片厂商和终端厂商已逐步加大投入。
- 1． **规模组网**
PoC完全依托公共运营商的4G/5G网络实现覆盖，客户无需自建任何基础设施，通过订阅服务即可快速开通，具有低CAPEX、弹性扩容、按需付费的优势，适合轻资产运营和快速启动。也可根据需求私有化部署。
MCX支持公网、行业专网、混合网络部署模式，公网模式需配置QoS策略，专网模式需自建基站和核心网、投入较高，但可实现覆盖自主可控、盲区快速补盲，混合模式则兼顾覆盖范围和保障等级，组网灵活性更强。同时也可支持OTT部署，纯IP接入不依赖核心网部署，与普通应用类似，服务质量取决于网络质量，不具备QoS保障机制。
- 1． **安全性**
PoC的安全机制主要依赖运营商4G/5G网络的空口加密，应用层安全由各家厂商自行实现，水平参差不齐，安全等级一般满足企业日常办公需求。

PMR/LMR运行在独立窄带专网，与民用宽带完全隔离，无线域内资源自主可控。
在专用或混合网络部署下，MCX通过3GPP标准化的QoS策略和优先级抢占机制，可在网络拥塞时保障关键会话不中断。纯公网部署时，效果取决于运营商的优先级策略配置。OTT部署则不具备该特性。
- 1． **互操作性**
PMR/LMR跨厂商、跨标准（如TETRA与P25之间）的互通需要专用网关，基本仅限语音业务。
MCX基于3GPP全球统一标准，支持多厂商互通。通过IWF（Interworking Function，互操作功能）可与现有PMR/LMR系统无缝互联，实现平滑过渡。
- 1． **系统过渡路径**
大多数行业的宽带升级都是渐进式落地。多数机构会保留原有PMR/LMR系统保障关键语音不间断，同时引入MCX关键任务通信，承载宽带协同业务、拓展广域覆盖。
依托标准化互通网关等宽窄融合互通方案，各单位可在过渡期实现两套系统并行调度，无需一次性关停原有系统、中断业务。
- 1． **安全性**
PMR/LMR安全主要依赖空口加密和物理网络隔离，安全模型相对封闭。
MCX采用符合3GPP标准的安全架构和机制，支持端到端加密，能够有效防止数据泄露、篡改和未经授权的访问。且兼容性强，能与其他符合该标准的系统在同样的安全机制下进行互操作。
- 1． **成本与演进**
PMR/LMR采用高CAPEX（资本支出）自建模式，但生命周期长（10-15年）。设备供应商正在逐步减少对传统技术的支持，新建项目趋于萎缩。
MCX采用低CAPEX、灵活OPEX模式，支持软件持续迭代。3GPP标准持续演进，可融入AI、6G等前沿技术。
### 1.3 应用场景

MCX基于5GC专用承载与默认承载的差异说明 V1.0
## 1 专用承载与默认承载
MCX基于5GC的专用承载是3GPP标准组织为MCX关键任务引入的用户面流量QoS Flow（即承载），并定义了专用QoS标识，为强制性标准要求，符合MCX关键任务的业务特点，确保MCX关键任务执行时具备QoS保障和高优先处理能力。
默认承载通常使用5GC定义常见的QoS标识（如：5QI 9），采用Non-GBR资源类型，优先级等级较低（如5QI=9，其优先级最低），网络采用尽力而为的模式，所有交互数据使用同一个承载传输，无QoS保障和优先级处理能力，与MCX专用承载存在本质性差异。
## 2 核心差异
|   序号 | 维度            | MCX专载                                                                                                                      | 默载                                                                    |
|------|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
|    1 | 专载标识5QI       | 3GPP标准引入MCX专用5QI=65（语音）、67（视频）、69（信令）、70（数据），不同的业务使用专用承载传输通道，确保业务随时随地可用                                                    | 通常使用优先级较低的5QI=9或8、6等标识，信令、语音、视频及数据业务、以及其它如邮件、网页、即时通信APP等使用同一个默认承载传输通道 |
|    2 | 资源类型          | 语音（65）和视频（67）为GBR，预留空口和网络资源，任何时候保证资源可用，可随时发起MCX业务                                                                          | 为Non-GBR，资源分配尽力而为，网络拥塞时业务出现卡顿、延时大、业务建立失败等现象，导致语音卡顿、听不清、视频花屏、业务失败等     |
|    3 | 优先级           | 专用5QI优先级（7、15、5、55），网络优先级高（如：5QI=65，5优先级最高），延迟可控，MCX业务在核心网资源优先调度处理                                                         | 优先级低（如：5QI=8 优先级为80，非常低）处理，业务资源调度延迟排队、资源竞争、资源被抢占等                     |

- 1． **网络底座**
PMR/LMR依托独立专用窄带无线组网，针对本地语音稳定性和自主运维管控深度优化；若要拓展覆盖范围、实现跨机构互通，则需重新规划频谱、落地工程施工，并配套互通网关设备。
MCX原生适配4G/5G网络，支持公网、行业专网、混合网络部署模式。宽带架构通过业务策略与QoS保障机制，在网络高负载下维持关键业务连续性。同时支持OTT部署，纯IP接入不依赖核心网部署，与普通应用类似，服务质量取决于网络质量，不具备QoS保障机制。
- 1． **系统架构**
PMR/LMR基础设施以硬件设备为核心：基站、直放站、调度控制器均为实体硬件；扩容或新增功能，往往需要新增硬件设备、配套完整工程实施周期。
MCX平台采用IMS灵活强大的业务框架，扩容、冗余部署、功能版本迭代均可通过软件受控升级完成，具体能力取决于部署方案。
- 1． **覆盖与部署**
PMR/LMR覆盖范围受限于自建基础设施，扩展需要复杂的频率规划和物理工程建设，跨区域互联互通困难。
MCX可利用现有公共4G/5G网络的广泛覆盖，并通过卫星接入（NTN）、网络切片等技术扩展覆盖，也可支持OTT方式，部署更加灵活。
- 1． **业务能力**
PMR/LMR数据带宽有限（常规业务为几kbps至几十kbps），底层架构以语音调度为核心，主要支持语音、短消息和简单状态信息，无法支持高清图片传输、实时视频回传。
MCX平台可承载全场景关键作业业务，同时原生支持MCPTT、MCVideo和MCData三大核心服务。这是MCX相对于PMR/LMR最显著的差异化优势。

query: MCX-5G专网中，MCX服务端通过哪几个接口与核心网网元对接？
agent_answer:
根据《MCSTARS产品白皮书V1.1.1》中“MCX基于5GC的网络框架”章节，MCX服务端（MCX Service，即AF，包含MCComm、MCPTT、MCVideo、MCData等网元）与5GC核心网网元对接的接口共有 **3 个：Rx、N5、N33**，均为QoS保证相关的交互接口。

| 接口 | 对端核心网网元 | 用途 |
|------|--------------|------|
| **Rx** | PCF | AF与PCF之间QoS保证相关的交互处理，即会话管理及MC专载管理 |
| **N5** | PCF | AF与PCF之间QoS保证相关的处理交互，即会话管理及MC专载管理 |
| **N33** | NEF | AF与NEF之间QoS保证相关的处理交互，即会话管理及MC专载管理 |

说明：上述接口中AF指IMS域中的SBC/P-CSCF或MCX域中的MCX Service。此外白皮书网络框架中还涉及ISC（与CSCF对接）、Sh（与HSS对接），属于与IMS核心网/用户数据网元的对接接口，不属于5GC核心网（PCF/NEF）对接范围。

补充佐证：在2025年第五届FRMCS互操作测试中，该MCX系统已基于N5参考点（及Rx）与华为、Telotronic、Kontron、Druid等厂商的5GC核心网完成集成对接。

### 2.4 关键技术
#### 2.4.1 遵循标准
- 基于3GPP R18协议标准；
- 持续演进，保证跟核心网和其他MCX系统互通互联。
#### 2.4.2 基于核心网
在4G/5G网络中，QoS定义了不同数据流的传输优先级、资源分配及性能保障机制，确保各类业务获得符合其需求的承载。QCI是QoS的分类标识（5G网络中叫5QI），以数字标识一组预定义的QoS特性（如：优先级、资源类型、允许的最大时延、允许的最大丢包率等），网络设备（如基站、核心网）根据QCI快速匹配预定义的QoS规则，应用相应的资源分配策略。下面两个表格分别是3GPP标准提供的4G网络中标准QCI分类和5G网络中的5QI分类，可以保证QCI值在不同厂商设备间通用，确保跨网络QoS一致性。
表 -1 4G网络的标准QCI分类
| QCI    | 资源类型    | 优先级     | 时延         | 丢包率            | 典型应用服务                                                                                                     |
|--------|---------|---------|------------|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1      | GBR     | 2       | 100 ms     | 10  -2         | Conversational Voice                                                                                       |
| 2      |         | 4       | 150 ms     | 10  -3         | Conversational Video (Live Streaming)                                                                      |
| 3      |         | 3       | 50 ms      | 10  -3         | Real Time Gaming, V2X messages  Electricity distribution - medium voltage  Process automation - monitoring |
| 4      |         | 5       | 300 ms     | 10  -6         | Non-Conversational Video (Buffered Streaming)                                                              |
| **65** |         | **0.7** | **75 ms**  | **10**  **-2** | **Mission Critical user plane Push To Talk voice (e.g., MCPTT)**                                           |
| 66     |         | 2       | 100 ms     | 10  -2         | Non-Mission-Critical user plane Push To Talk voice                                                         |

**移动客户端（MCClient）：** 基于安卓系统的关键任务客户端，提供客户端登录、语音、视频、多媒体数据等业务功能。
MCX系统支持3种组网方式：运营商4G/5G网络，4G/5G专网，OTT模式。
- 运营商4G/5G公网模式无需自建专网，有效降低了成本
符合3GPP标准设计，系统能力依赖于运营商网元的对接实现程度。
- 4G/5G专网模式，能提供更高效/更高质量的服务
符合3GPP标准设计，可以最大限度发挥MCX系统特性。
- OTT模式
OTT模式不依赖核心网；部署灵活，基于纯IP网络；接入灵活，适应更多应用场景：支持NON-3GPP各种网络及终端接入。
综上，由于MCX系统兼容多种组网方式，保证了覆盖范围不受限制，并能满足多样化通信应用场景的需求。
MCX系统支持跨MCX系统的业务互通，不同MCX系统的设备之间可以互通语音、视频和数据。

# Convergence and Interworking
Interworking between MCX Domain Users and VoNR Domain Users:
Users in the MCX domain and VoNR domain can act as the calling party and called party respectively to initiate or receive voice call requests, thus realizing interworking between users of the two domains.
For the mutual roaming between users in the MCX domain and VoNR domain, seamless roaming across the two domains can be achieved with the support of multi-mode terminals and on the premise of ensuring the consistency of user data.

#### 2.3.3 Network Architecture
The MCX system, evolving based on 3GPP standards, seamlessly interfaces with 4G/5G core networks.
##### 2.3.3.1 MCX Network Architecture Based on LTE
![image_1786159011080722.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159011082857_image_1786159011080722.png)
Figure 2.3-3 MCX Network Architecture Based on LTE
Reference Points:
**Rx:** This reference point is located between the AF(Application function) and the PCRF, used for QoS-guaranteed interaction processing, specifically for session management and MC dedicated bearer management between AF and PCRF. Here, AF refers to the SBC/P-CSCF in the IMS or the MCX Service in the MCX system.
**ISC:** This reference point is located between the S-CSCF and MCX Service, used to complete third-party registration, service authentication, subscription notification, session management, calls, short data messages, and other SIP protocol processing, routing, and media negotiation.
**Sh:** This reference point is located between the MCX Service and HSS. The MCX Service obtains user information, policy information, subscription information, and other data from the HSS through this reference point.
**LTE-Uu:** This reference point is located between the UE and the E-UTRAN wireless access network, used for interactions between the UE and the access network, including terminal registration, attachment, bearer management, QoS, priority, preemption, signaling exchange, and data transmission.
**S1-U:** This reference point is located between the E-UTRAN wireless access network and the SGW, used for user plane bearer channels and the switching of transmission paths between eNodeBs.
**SGi:** This reference point is located between the PGW and the packet data network, used for the data transmission and data exchange of control plane and media plane.
Note: MCX Service includes network elements such as MCComm, MCPTT, MCVideo, and MCData.
##### 2.3.3.2 MCX Network Architecture Based on 5GC
![image_1786159011086121.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159011088197_image_1786159011086121.png)
Figure 2.3-4 MCX Network Architecture Based on 5GC
Reference points:
**Rx:** This reference point is located between the AF and PCF, used for QoS-guaranteed interaction processing, specifically for session management and MC dedicated bearer management between AF and PCF. Here, AF refers to SBC/P-CSCF in the IMS or MCX Service in the MCX system.
**N5:** This reference point is located between the AF and PCF, used for QoS-guaranteed interaction processing, specifically for session management and MC dedicated bearer management between AF and PCF. Here, AF refers to SBC/P-CSCF in the IMS or MCX Service in the MCX system.
**N33:** This reference point is located between the AF and NEF, used for QoS-guaranteed interaction processing, specifically for session management and MC dedicated bearer management between AF and NEF. Here, AF refers to SBC/P-CSCF in the IMS or MCX Service in the MCX system.
**ISC:** This reference point is located between the CSCF and MCX Service, used for SIP protocol processing, including third-party registration, service authentication, subscription notifications, session management, calls, short messages, routing, and media negotiation.
**Sh:** This reference point is located between the MCX Service and HSS. The MCX Service retrieves user data, policy information, subscription details, and other data from the HSS through this reference point.

“N”种业务特性：依托点对点呼叫、群组呼叫、动态组管理、数据共享、应急调度等核心特性，在满足客户宽带化群组通信、数据信息安全保障、跨部门系统协同等需求的基础上，同步提供全流程调度与管理能力。 ### 2.2 关键技术 #### 2.2.1 “1” 套基础底座 为同时满足公共安全、运输、能源及其他关键任务行业在语音、视频、数据通信等场景下对高质量、高可靠、高安全的核心诉求，以及各关键任务行业间互联互通、协同运作的发展需求，MCX 系统通过统一的基础底座为上层 MCPTT、MCVideo、MCData 等多媒体应用提供业务支撑能力。 MCX 组网架构一般由 MCX 客户端、5G 核心网、SIP 核心网、应用服务器（MC 服务器、MC 用户数据库、MC 网关服务器）四部分组成，如图 3 所示：
图 3 MCX 端到端网络架构图
图中各模块分别介绍如下： ## · MCX 客户端（MCX UE） MCX 客户端作为 MCX 网络的接入入口，需具备单呼、组呼、高优先级呼叫及呼叫抢占等核心功能，通过实现关键任务通信优先保障、用户身份安全绑定、开机一键快速注册等能力，全面适配公共安全、紧急响应、灾害救援等场景对通信高可靠、低延迟、快接入的核心诉求。 ## · 5G 核心网（5GC） 5G 核心网作为 MCX 网络的“高速公路”，依托低延迟通信、广播组播、QoS 保障、移动性管理、安全通信等特性，为 MCX 网络提供网络资源保障以及稳定、可靠、低延迟的数据传输。 ## · SIP 核心网（SIP core） SIP Core 作为 MCX 网络的“调度中心”，由标准或简化的 IMS 核心网构成，包含多个逻辑单元；提供代理路由、SIP 加密、业务和应用服务器选择、用户注册管理等功能。

#### 2.4.3 微服务架构
![image_1786159015899151.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159015900996_image_1786159015899151.png)

MCX系统基于微服务化架构，平台组件间耦合性降至最低，支持多实例集群化部署。
产品支持容器化部署，极大提升开发、部署与运维效率。
部署操作支持一键部署脚本。
系统采用无状态服务设计理念，这种设计方式极大地提升了单台节点的并发处理能力。由于无状态服务不需要在服务器端保存客户端的会话状态信息，服务器可以更高效地处理多个客户端的请求，减少了服务器的处理负担。同时，这种设计降低了服务器的成本，无论是硬件成本还是运营成本都得到了有效控制，为系统的大规模部署和长期运行提供了经济、高效的解决方案。

query: MCX-MCX_OTT部署特点？
gold_answer: 基于IP层接入MCX网络，无业务QoS保障，通信可靠性依赖网络质量
agent_answer:
MCX 的 OTT 部署是指 MCX 系统作为 IP 网络上的应用服务运行，不依赖 4G/5G 核心网。知识库中对其部署特点的记载如下：

## OTT 部署特点

**1. 部署形态**
- MCX 系统作为 IP 网络上的应用服务，不依赖核心网部署（可避免法律政策风险）。
- 不需要 IMS/SIP Core 与底层 LTE/5G 基础设施之间的任何绑定。
- 纯 IP 接入，部署灵活。

**2. 底层网络的角色与限制**
- 任何底层网络（例如 LTE/5G、WiFi 或以太网等有线技术）仅提供基本的数据传输能力（即接入层网络提供传输通道）。
- 底层网络不提供 QoS/优先级执行，也不提供接入层的多播/广播能力（即不支持单播 PCC 或 LTE/5G 中的多播机制）。
- 该模式下不支持核心网 QoS、单播及多播。

**3. 接入能力**
- 支持 NON-3GPP 各种网络及终端接入，接入灵活、适用面广。
- 该模式下普通终端也可接入。
- 基于 IMS 网络架构。
- 网络兼容性好，可适应更多应用场景。

MCX域用户与VoNR域用户互通：

# 双网融合
宽窄带网融合
TETRA 和 P25 等 LMR 系统被全球公共安全机构广泛部署。这些窄带系统已经使用了二十多年。因此，MCX 服务标准替换传统技术可能需要几年时间,通过LMR 和 MCX 系统之间基于标准的互操作来解决这个遗留问题。
3GPP在第16版中完成了与LMR系统互通的标准化，即IWF网管实现宽窄带融合，为MCPTT和MCData服务与传统LMR系统互通所需的基本功能提供了一个框架。

在一些特定行业（如铁路、公共安全等）中，MCX系统可以部署在专用网络中。例如，铁路5G专网可以按照铁路局进行部署，每个路局设置自己的核心网和MCX集群通信系统。这种部署方式能够更好地满足行业特定的需求，提供更高的安全性和可靠性。
#### 2.7.3 OTT部署
![image_1786159015992510.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159015994907_image_1786159015992510.png)
图 2.7-5 OTT部署
OTT部署方式下，MCX系统作为IP网络上的应用服务。这种部署方式下，任何底层网络（例如：LTE/5G、wifi或以太网等有线技术）仅提供基本的数据传输能力，不提供QoS/优先级执行或接入层的多播/广播能力（即也不支持单播PCC或LTE/5G中的多播机制）。不需要IMS/SIP core与底层LTE/5G基础设施之间的任何绑定。
### 2.8 宽窄带融合
MCX系统通过IWF网关与目前全球公共安全机构广泛使用的窄带通信系统：TETRA（由ETSI标准管理）和P25（由TIA-102标准管理）等LMR系统实现互联互通，可以进行语音组呼、紧急呼叫、端到端加密呼叫、动态重组、半双工单呼的互操作，确保关键通信的连续性和可靠性。

#### 3.1.1 公共安全领域
![image_1786159016008388.png](http://localhost:9000/public/kb_mvng8u1201/kb-images/1786159016011002_image_1786159016008388.png)
##### 3.1.1.1 需求分析
随着经济社会的不断发展和国际国内形势的复杂变化，公安机关维护国家安全和社会稳定的任务愈加艰巨繁重，任何情况下都要求能够完成任务和履行使命，关键通信显得尤为重要。依靠专网通信，容易受使用频段申请，接入许可、建网投入、施工周期、覆盖范围、网络运维等多方约束，专网建设整个过程需要大量人力和物力、以及后续维护成本，效益低下，而带宽大、速率高、覆盖广，无需申请频点的公网，无需专门建设运维，具备高度的抗毁容灾能力和安全性，提供语音、多媒体通信渠道的公网对讲成为公共安全领域关键通信一个有效的选择。

query: MCX-MCX SIP Core组件的功能是？
gold_answer: 提供核心网IP网络访问注册、鉴权、第三方注册、注册状态管理、会话发起、保持及释放管理、呼叫路由
agent_answer:
MCX SIP Core 是 MCX 产品组件之一，是基于 IP 网络的多媒体核心网组件。它与 4G/5G 核心网配合，向用户提供语音、视频、文本、图片等多媒体通信服务；在 MCX 组网架构中作为"调度中心"，由标准或简化的 IMS 核心网构成，包含多个逻辑单元。

**主要功能如下：**

| 功能类别 | 具体功能 |
|---|---|
| 注册与鉴权 | 核心网 IP 网络访问注册、鉴权、第三方注册、注册状态管理 |
| 会话控制 | 会话发起、保持及释放管理 |
| 路由 | 呼叫路由、代理路由 |
| 融合 | 移动与固网融合 |
| 媒体管理 | 媒体传输、转发、编解码管理 |
| 承载管理 | 承载管理 |
| 用户管理 | 签约用户管理 |
| 安全与业务选择 | SIP 加密、业务和应用服务器选择 |

MCData: Mission Critical Data Service, supports text short messages, multimedia short messages, file distribution, storage, and data streaming capacibility, provides mission critical multimedia data communication functions: one-to-one messages, group messages, file distribution, emergency messages, emergency alert, data streaming, IP connectivity, etc.
MCSipCore: Mission Critical SIP Core Service, based on IP multimedia network architecture services along with core networks, supports multimedia communication services including voice, video, text, image, etc. And supports functions: core network IP network registration, authentication, third-party registration, registration status management, session initiation/maintenance/release, call routing, fixed-mobile network convergence, media transmission/forwarding/codec management, bearer management, and subscriber management, etc.
MCCMDsip: Mission Critical Command Management & Dispatch Service, supports command & dispatch functions: blacklisting, presence monitoring, forced insertion, forced disconnection, ambient listening/viewing, video pushing/pulling, etc.
MCMRS: Mission Critical Recording and Replay Service, supports storage, viewing, exporting, retrieval, and playback for mission-critical logs, voice recordings, video recordings, multimedia data, etc.
MCLMS: Mission Critical Location Management Service, supports mission critical location management functions: device location reports, location information subscription/notification, and historical trajectory, etc.
MCKMS: Mission Critical Key Management Service, supports mission-critical key management, distribution, application, encrypted transmission for signaling/media data, etc.
MCMDM: Mission Critical Mobile Devices Management Service, supports batch control of mobile terminal applications, routine maintenance, security and task management, etc.
MCOAM: Mission Critical Operations Administration and Maintenance Service, supports tenants, permissions, users, resource management, business policies, logs, billing, etc.
MCNMS: Mission Critical Network Management, supports management of mission critical system deployment, network topology, performance monitoring, fault detection, alarms, security, log auditing, visualisation, etc.
MCDisp: Mission Critical Web Dispatch, based on web visual command & dispatch client provides functions including: user login, voice communication, video communication, multimedia data communication, dispatching, GIS-based visual operations, etc.
MCIWF: Mission Critical InterWorking Function Gateway, provides inter-system interworking gateway function, e.g., interworking with LMR narrowband system.
MCClient: Mission Critical Client, based on Android mission critical client, provides functions including: user login, voice communication, video communication, multimedia data communication, etc.
The MCX system supports three networking methods: 4G/5G operator network mode, 4G/5G private network mode, and OTT mode.
**4G/5G operator network mode**
This model effectively reduces costs by eliminating the need to build your own dedicated network. Designed in compliance with 3GPP standards, the system's capabilities depend on the integration level achieved with operator network elements.
**4G/5G private network mode**
This mode can provide more efficient/higher quality services. It is designed in accordance with the 3GPP standard, which can maximize the performance of the MCX system.
**OTT mode**
The OTT mode is independent of the core network, it features flexible deployment based on a pure IP network, and offers flexible access, adapting to a wider range of application scenarios, it supports access from various non-3GPP networks and terminals.
In summary, the MCX system's compatibility with multiple networking modes ensures unrestricted coverage and meets the requirements of diverse communication application scenarios.
The MCX system supports service interoperability across different MCX systems, enabling voice, video, and data exchange between devices from different MCX systems.

MCComm
MCComm provides core MC user services, including authentication, service authorization, and token distribution to ensure secure system access. It also manages user/service/terminal/group configuration and state publication, subscription, and notification.
SIP Core
An IP-based multimedia core that, integrated with the 4G/5G core network, delivers voice, video and other multimedia services. It handles registration, authentication, session control, call routing, mobile-fixed convergence, media management, bearer control and subscriber management.
MCPTT Voice
MCPTT delivers mission-critical voice communication services, supporting full-duplex calls, private/group PTT, emergency alerts, group re-organization, ad-hoc/group broadcasting, and group chat.
Dispatch Service
As the mission-critical dispatch service, it delivers mission-critical dispatch functions including status presentation, blacklist management, remote stun/kill/revive, forced call tear-down/insert/pull-out/eject, microphone mute, dispatch console monitoring (audio/video), environment monitoring (audio/video), video push/forwarding/backhaul.
MCVideo
MCVideo delivers mission-critical video communication services, including video private call, video group call, emergency video private /group call, emergency alerts, group reconfiguration, ad-hoc group calls.
Recording Service
As the mission-critical audio and video recording service, it provides logging for voice, video calls, short messages and dispatcher operations, including voice call recording, video call recording, caller/callee information, timestamps, call duration logs, and dispatcher operation records.

- 1、 **与LMR互通：**
1. 采用背靠背硬件网关，实现语音互通，MCX与网关直接通过SIP协议对接（主推，成本可控，能够快速部署系统，无知识产权风险）；
2. 支持基于3GPP标准的IWF方案，实现MCX与LMR互通。方案集成主流IWF产品厂家的设备，实现MCX与LMR系统的平滑融合。标准IWF方案需要协调LMR系统厂家的对接支持，以及不低的对接费用。目前，市场上IWF厂家少、产品少、价格高，同时需要LMR原厂协议、安全及数据对接支持，技术复杂、难度大，对接费用高，实施周期长。
## 4 终端
系统：小屏终端Android6及以上，大屏智能终端Android8及以上；
专载：UE需支持MCX DNN接入和访问。UE需支持标准QoS机制，支持MCX的专用承载，包括语音专用承载（5QI=65）、视频专用承载（5QI=67）、信令专用承载（5QI=69）和多媒体数据专用承载（5QI=70）。

MCX常见问题
## 1 关于部署
### 1.1 RPO/RTO
| 部署方式               |  RPO     | RTO   | 备注   |
|--------------------|----------|-------|------|
| 本地 1+1 部署          | 30s      | 60s   |      |
| 本地 1+0 部署及 私有云上的灾备 | 60s      | 2分钟   |      |
| 私有云上采用 1+1 部署      | 2分钟      | 3分钟   |      |
1、RTO 恢复时间目标 Recovery Time Objective
含义：系统故障宕机后，最多允许业务中断多久、多长时间内必须恢复正常运行。
例：RTO=30 分钟 → 系统崩了，必须在 30 分钟内修好上线，业务不能停超半小时。
侧重：停机最长容忍时长。
2、RPO 恢复点目标 Recovery Point Objective
含义：故障发生后，最多能丢失多长时间的数据，能回溯到哪个时间点的数据。
例：RPO=15 分钟 → 最多丢最近 15 分钟新增数据，恢复后数据只截止到故障前 15 分钟。
侧重：数据最大丢失量。
### 1.2 虚拟化
- 1． 是否支持虚拟化平台（VMware 、 OpenStack） ？
都支持，在虚拟化平台内 可以虚拟出虚拟机安装ubuntu 系统。 然后安装MCX服务。
## 2 规格指标
### 2.1 业务规格
- 1． 调度系统单文件上传最大支持多大？
文件上传大小上限不超过 3GB。
### 2.2 数据存储
系统超管可统一设置用户登录记录、呼叫记录、录音&录像记录、多媒体数据记录等服务开关，默认数据存储时长 90 天，可手动配置 1~365 天，也可按项目需求个性化定制。
当前暂不支持针对每个租户的单独设置。
## 3 关于集成互联
### 3.1 二次开发接口
当前有以下二次开发接口：
1. Windows Web调度台接口：有Js SDK和Demo，暂无文档；
2. 服务端管理接口：群组管理类SDK接口，有文档；
3. 安卓端接口：安卓SDK及Demo，MCPTT、MCVideo、MCData，有文档。
### 3.2 第三方互联
- 1、 **支持与第三方SIP电话互联互通**
SIP协议方式对接，实现全双工通话。

MCX采用符合3GPP标准的安全架构和机制，支持端到端加密，能够有效防止数据泄露、篡改和未经授权的访问。且兼容性强，能与其他符合该标准的系统在同样的安全机制下进行互操作。
- 1． **宽窄融合**
PoC作为独立的应用层服务，无法直接与TETRA、PDT、P25等窄带集群系统对接，若客户已有LMR投资，需额外采购专用网关且功能受限，通常仅能支持语音互通，数据和视频无法跨系统流转。
MCX在3GPP标准中明确定义了IWF互操作功能，可实现与LMR系统的标准化对接，帮助客户在保护既有投资的同时平滑向宽带演进。
- 1． **业务框架**
PoC的业务能力以语音对讲为核心，部分厂商扩展了定位、图文消息、视频通话等功能，但均为私有实现，无统一标准保障，视频和数据能力在质量、时延、可靠性方面取决于网络质量，适合简单工作协同场景。
MCX定义了三大标准化服务——MCPTT（关键任务一键通）、MCVideo（关键任务视频）、MCData（关键任务数据），每项服务均有明确的QoS指标、信令流程和优先级机制，可实现语音、视频、数据的一体化融合调度，支撑复杂业务场景。
- 1． **系统演进**
公网PoC：功能迭代依赖厂商自身规划，无统一技术演进路线。
MCX：依托3GPP标准持续迭代，R17已支持卫星接入（NTN），R18引入AI增强，未来可平滑升级至5G-A及6G，是行业未来十年关键通信的统一演进底座。
### 2.3 应用场景
| 场景              | 推荐方案        | 原因                                      |
|-----------------|-------------|-----------------------------------------|
| 警察、消防、急救指挥      | MCX         | 通信失败=生命损失                               |
| 铁路/地铁调度、港口/机场运营 | MCX         | 视频+数据是刚需，网络级保障  3GPP已定义铁路FRMCS标准替代GSM-R |

MCX基于3GPP全球统一标准，不同厂商设备可天然互通，同时通过标准化的IWF（Interworking Function）互操作功能，能够与存量LMR窄带集群系统实现语音、数据、控制信令的双向互通，支持宽窄融合调度，特别适合需要跨部门、跨区域、跨系统协同的复杂指挥场景。
- 1． **产业链**
PoC的产业链成熟度较高，终端侧可利用市面上绝大多数通用对讲机、智能手机、执法仪、平板、三防/车载终端，芯片和模组供应链成熟且成本极低，客户选择面广、更换成本低，这使其能够快速渗透企业市场。
MCX的产业链相对聚焦于专用领域，终端需通过3GPP合规认证，芯片和模组成本较高，但产业链正在随着全球公共安全宽带化建设持续扩展，主流通信芯片厂商和终端厂商已逐步加大投入。
- 1． **规模组网**
PoC完全依托公共运营商的4G/5G网络实现覆盖，客户无需自建任何基础设施，通过订阅服务即可快速开通，具有低CAPEX、弹性扩容、按需付费的优势，适合轻资产运营和快速启动。也可根据需求私有化部署。
MCX支持公网、行业专网、混合网络部署模式，公网模式需配置QoS策略，专网模式需自建基站和核心网、投入较高，但可实现覆盖自主可控、盲区快速补盲，混合模式则兼顾覆盖范围和保障等级，组网灵活性更强。同时也可支持OTT部署，纯IP接入不依赖核心网部署，与普通应用类似，服务质量取决于网络质量，不具备QoS保障机制。
- 1． **安全性**
PoC的安全机制主要依赖运营商4G/5G网络的空口加密，应用层安全由各家厂商自行实现，水平参差不齐，安全等级一般满足企业日常办公需求。

U_{E} UIC .uns de fer) User Equipment International union of railways (Union Internationale des Chemins de fer) ### 4. Technical and Project Management ### 4.1 Scope The main goal of the ninth MCX Plugtests was testing the interoperability of the MCPTT, MCData and MCVideo ecosystem signalling and media plane at different levels. The Multi-client scenarios, Off-Network, Inter MCX, Multicast and interworking (IWF) with LMR were tested during the event. The basic scenario tested comprised MCX application server(s) - both controlling and participating- and multiple MCX clients deployed over a generic SIP/IMS core, LTE & 5G access network with and without MCX required PCC capabilities with native multicast support (i.e. Release-14 - and higher- eMBMS) and UEs. The following Figure 1 illustrates the basic test infrastructure. Additionally, off-network communications between two UEs using 5G sidelink was evaluated.
### Figure 1. Typical MCPTT/MCData/MCVideo scenario to be considered in the Plugtests In the scope of this Plugtests event, the following high level test objectives were performed. - Connectivity (CONN): Tests covered basic connectivity between functional elements at different levels including Access Network (LTE), IP Network, SIP/IMS and MCPTT/MCData/MCVideo Application level. At LTE level, unicast and more particularly eMBMS multicast connectivity was evaluated. Tests at IP layer targeted pure OTT connectivity regardless the underlying access network. SIP connectivity tests checked proper deployment of MCX AS over the selected SIP Core/IMS so that all SIP messages were successfully delivered from MCX Clients to Participating/Controlling MCPTT Servers and vice versa. In this 9th Plugtests, AS vendors provided their own built-in SIP/IMS cores so that Clients registered into different cores depending on the specific test session. Application level refers to e2e signalling, media, floor controlling (and other involved) protocols in use. Plugtests participants were encouraged to carry on CONN tests over Mission Critical LTE/5G for unicast – or UNI-MC-LTE/5G – and Mission Critical LTE with multicast eMBMS capabilities – so called MULTI-MC-LTE. Additionally, low level configuration-specific details (i.e. MCPTT, MC QCI and eMBMS bearer management) were considered in the PCC and eMBMS specific objectives. MCData and MCVideo fea tures were mostly analysed in test cases associated to the CONN objective while sibling procedures (i.e. registration to different MCPTT/MCData/MCVideo servers) were carried out when needed. - eMBMS (EMBMS): Comprised checking of eMBMS specific signalling both in the MB2-U/C interface and e2e. - Multi IOP: Interoperability testing-oriented complex test cases were added for Multi-client scenarios. - Interworking Function (IWF): MCPTT connectivity test cases were re-used to test interworking with LMR systems (Tetra and P25). - Inter MCX: MCPTT/MCVideo connectivity test cases were used to test interworking between application servers. Off-Network: MCPTT off network test cases were used to test direct mode communication using Sidelink UEs. ### 4.2 Timeline The preparation was run through different phases as described in the Figure 2 below.

Handling of SIM cards. Due to the large number of participants, multiple 4G EPC and 5G Core providers, and the seven test streams (A through G), the number of SIM cards and the eventual need to swap them for different test sessions depending on the number of UEs available per MCX client vendor demand a careful handling and tracking by the participants. The deployment of three 4G networks (Bands 38/40) and four 5G networks (Band 78) further increased the complexity of SIM card management. Although no issues or complaints were finally reported to the ETSI team, a unified or systematic approach for the abovementioned handling is deemed useful.
Need for frequency management. The deployment of multiple 4G and 5G radio equipment across seven networks required a proper management of the spectrum to be used, requesting the proper permission from ARCEP (the French spectrum regulator) and coordinating in specific frequency bands, namely Bands 38, and 40 for 4G and Band 78 for 5G.
Usage of specific test-related PLMN IDs. Some commercial devices either ban or already have an OEM hard-coded configuration for test PLMN IDs (such as 001 01). This was announced in advance but, anyway, some EPC and 5GC providers decided to change the typical configuration to prevent any problems during the face-to-face event. Unique PLMN IDs should be used for each 4G or 5G network present in the Plugtests and support of these PLMN IDs must be supported by the UEs.
Provisioning information. In the internal WIKI page for the 10th MCX Plugtests specific provisioning information was shared to help the interoperability and reduce the preparation needed for every test session, including PLMN IDs to be used, details for the domains/realms, Application Server information, and conventions for SIP/IMS and MCX identities and functional aliases. However, the availability of bootstrapping mechanisms, the usage of Managed Objects (MOs) according to ETSI TS 124 383 or the adoption by the vendors of off-line (i.e. using MDM/OTA/TP or any other) automated provisioning method is not homogeneous in vendor implementations, making the final configuration mechanism mostly manual and therefore slow and error prone, consuming a non-negligible part of the test sessions, especially in those involving multiple clients and/or servers.
Role of the SIP/IMS cores and SIM cards. Similarly to the previous, the usage of SIM based authentication and derivation of SIP identities and realms from the ISIM within the physical SIM card for SIP registration and IMS-AKA based authentication is still not available in many MCX clients/UE vendors. Similarly, the automated discovery of PCSCF from the 4G or 5G network signalling was not used. Instead, manual configuration for every SIP/IMS core registrar server was needed, leading again to delays.
MTU and fragmentation issues. The testing setups typically involve connecting to components in different networks (4G, 5G, Ethernet, VPN) even remotely through the ETSI HIVE, with different MTU sizes. Since there is no agreed PMTU discovery mechanism in place and sometimes the MCX components do/can not properly control the Don't Fragment (DF bit) capabilities in IP datagrams there typically appear hard-to-troubleshoot connectivity issues. MCSTARS 产品是基于 **3GPP Release 18** 标准协议开发的，并随标准更新持续演进、向前兼容未来版本。

**知识库依据：**

1. **产品介绍资料**：《MCSTARS Product Introduction-V1.1.1.pptx》中明确记载："MCSTARS is a next-generation mission-critical communication system developed based on **3GPP Release 18 standards**. It comprises three standardized service subsystems: MCPTT, MCVideo and MCData"，即 MCSTARS 是基于 3GPP Release 18 标准开发的下一代关键任务通信系统，包含 MCPTT、MCVideo、MCData 三大标准化业务子系统，提供语音、视频、数据多媒体集群业务。

2. **销售速查手册**：《MCSTARS Sales Quick Guide (Internal Use) V1.1.1》在"标准合规与向前兼容"部分记载：系统"Developed based on **3GPP Release 18 and above**"，采用全球统一协议，随标准更新持续迭代，完全兼容未来版本和网络协议，消除技术过时风险。

**补充背景**（来自《面向关键任务的群组通信（MCX）技术白皮书》）：3GPP 已完成 Release 12 至 Release 18 的 MCX 标准化制定，Release 19 正在进行；其中基于 LTE 的商用版本在 Release 16，**基于 5G 的商用版本在 Release 18**。

## 1 Overview
### 1.1 Document Overview
This white paper is dedicated to the MCSTARS broadband trunking communications solution (MCSTARS for short), offering a comprehensive and in-depth analysis of the system from a structured and holistic perspective. It details the solution's accurate positioning, distinctive features, scientifically optimized architecture, cutting-edge core technologies, versatile functionality, rigorous technical specifications, and a wide range of representative use cases. By providing an all-encompassing interpretation, this document aims to help users gain a thorough understanding of the MCSTARS system, accurately assess its value, and make informed business decisions supported by practical insights.
### 1.2 Company Profile
POCSTARS, founded in 2010, is a pioneering solution and service provider in the field of communication command and dispatch. The company is committed to advancing trunking communication technologies and industry-focused solutions. Headquartered in Shenzhen, it has established R&D and customer support centers in Shijiazhuang, Xi'an, and Qingdao, with multiple overseas offices supporting global business expansion.
POCSTARS, a global solution brand under the company, offers a range of solutions tailored for different markets: POCSTARS-MNO is designed for telecom carriers, POCSTARS-PRO targets the Small and Medium-sized Enterprise (SME) market, POCSTARS-UC serves industry clients, and MCSTARS complies with the 3GPP MCX standards. Additionally, POCSTARS' geo-location solution is specifically designed for precise industry-level positioning. Guided by the vision of "Connecting New Frontiers", POCSTARS geo-location platform integrates various technologies such as push-to-talk (PTT) terminals, broadband and narrowband trunking communication networks, next-generation command and dispatch systems, public telephone services, IoT devices, video surveillance, multi-mode positioning technologies, 3D GIS, and AI-driven computer vision. This results in a highly capable, integrated command and dispatch platform that delivers information convergence, decision support, and diverse features, and ensures reliable, secure communications, significantly enhancing coordination and operational efficiency.

Permission System: Role-based access control for pages and functions.
Group Management: Edit groups, members and configurations; support quick group creation via templates.
Device & Service Management: Configure MCX services, access, map and manage SIP terminals in bulk to enable communication across heterogeneous terminals.
License Management: Support download, approval, import and update of License certificates.
### 4.3 Core Voice Services
Basic Calls: Full-duplex/half-duplex individual calls, first-answer calls, auto/manual call answering and call forwarding; compatible with AMR-WB codec.
Group Calls: Regular group calls, chat groups, ad-hoc group calls, late join, free entry & exit and voice broadcast; support call volume threshold policies.
Emergency Voice: Highest-priority emergency individual/group calls, one-click upgrade for regular calls and service downgrade linkage under emergency status.
Talk Permit Control: Exclusive talk permit, time limit, talk permit queuing, high-priority preemption and multi-party simultaneous speaking.
Emergency Alert: Group and individual SOS alerts with push of staff, location and organization information.
### 4.4 Core Video Services
Support auto/manual answering, full-duplex video individual calls and video group calls with late join and free entry & exit. It features video push, remote pull and targeted distribution to meet visualized dispatching requirements.
### 4.5 Multimedia & Data Services
Support point-to-point and group bidirectional transmission of text, voice, images, short videos, locations and files. Compatible with offline message cache and automatic download of small files for lightweight data interaction.
### 4.6 Visual Dispatching & Command
Status Monitoring: Real-time display of online status, emergency status, call status and alert status for all contacts and groups.
Emergency Dispatching: Remote silent environment monitoring, pop-up emergency alerts and tiered callback reminders.
Record & Traceability: Recording for audio & video calls, logs for all calls and multimedia services, and file playback & query.
Location Dispatching: Real-time location display and historical track playback via GIS for personnel situation management.
## 5 Core Advantages
- **High Reliability & Security**
When deployed on carrier networks, it adopts 3GPP QoS mechanisms to guarantee priority and resource reservation for mission-critical services, ensuring normal transmission of high-priority data amid network congestion.
Compliant with 3GPP security frameworks, it supports end-to-end signaling and application encryption to avoid data leakage and tampering. It enables interoperation with standard-compliant systems, and adopts hierarchical user authentication and authorization to strictly control access to core services.
- **Multi-vendor Interoperability**
Our devices have passed three major international interconnection tests: the 9th & 10th ETSI MCX Tests and the 5th FRMCS Test.
It also connects with non-3GPP PTT systems such as TETRA and P25. Standard APIs enable cross-system data sharing and maximize the utilization of existing devices.
- **Standard Compliance & Forward Compatibility**
Developed based on 3GPP Release 18 and above, the system adopts global unified protocols and iterates alongside standard updates. It is fully compatible with future versions and network protocols to eliminate technical obsolescence risks and ensure long-term serviceability.
In 2025, we jointly released the White Paper on Mission-Critical Group Communication (MCX) with China Mobile Research Institute. As a member of CCSA, we deeply participate in formulating the domestic standard General Technical Requirements for 5G Mission-Critical (MCX) Communication Systems, which has been officially approved as an industry standard project.

## 10 Plugtests Observations As a result of the Plugtests event activities some issues in 3GPP Technical Specifications (TSs) and related standards were identified together with practical deployment problems that may demand some clarification or feedback from the related SDOs. We have classified those aspects into the following two categories: Observations to MCX Standards: Missing, erroneous or ambiguous definition of procedures in 3GPP's MCPTT TSs. - Technical constraints: Related to implementation issues, not covered by the standards, but which need to be faced by MCX vendors in most deployments. The reader should note that 3GPP Release 18 was considered for the ninth MCX Plugtests event. The $ 9^{th} $ MCX Plugtests event team wants to thank all the participants in the Plugtests for kindly sharing the following lessons learned. Specific actions towards pushing this feedback to relevant TSGs in 3GPP have already been started at the time of the release of this report. ### 10.1 Observations #### 10.1.1 Lack of explicit description of FD dynamics for interMCX scenarios Trusted mode has been removed from MCData Stage 3 in 3GPPT TS 24.282 for SDS and MCVideo 3GPP TS 24.281 (while it's kept for MCPTT and a specific reference to that for MCVideo is included in 9.2.1.5.2.2 in TS 24.281) but there's no reference to the behaviour of an eventual non-controlling controlling server for FD operations. Plugtests participants would like to request 3GPP CT1 for clarification regarding whether such mechanism is eventually considered for MCData FD. [EDITORIAL] Additionally, note that there's a typo assuming MCVideo (instead of MCData) in Section 9.2.2.5 ####### 10.1.2 Unclear mapping of MCVideo Transmission Control timers in TS 24.483 and mismatches between TS 24.483 and TS 24.484 In TS 24.581- Section 11 (Table 11.1.1-1, Table 11.1.3-1, Table 11.1.4-1) MCVideo Transmission Control related timers are defined. However, either they are not defined in the TS 24.484 or they are referenced to TS 24.483 and "shared" with MCPTT. Plugtests participants would like to request 3GPP CT1 for clarification regarding the use in TS 24.483 of the same name timers for MCPTT/MCVideo (i.e. T100, T101...) and/or otherwise include the definitions in TS 24.483 and TS 24.484 of MCVideo timers and missing tags (i.e. T2-transmission-idle, T3-transmission-revoke, T4-transmission-granted...).

The reader should note that 3GPP Release 19 was considered for the tenth MCX Plugtests event.
The  $ 10^{th} $ MCX Plugtests event team wants to thank all the participants in the Plugtests for kindly sharing the following lessons learned. Specific actions towards pushing this feedback to relevant TSGs in 3GPP have already been started at the time of the release of this report.
### 10.1 Observations
#### 10.1.1 Unknown behaviour of the participating and targeted client when sending/receiving location reporting configuration
Clause 13.2.2 in 3GPPT TS 24.379 and 13.3.2.1 (both referenced from other sections) do not state the expected behaviour upon submission/reception of SIP MESSAGE for location reporting configuration.
#### 10.1.2 Non explicit behaviour of the LMC when receiving LocationConfiguration notification
Clause 6.2.2.5.2 in 3GPPT TS 24.283 does not define how the LMC should answer to the LocationConfiguration POST from the LMS (204 assumed).
############# 10.1.3 Typo or unclear behaviour upon reception of location notification request  Final steps of 6.2.2.7.2 in 3GPPT TS 24.283 have either a typo or an unclear behaviour. The yaml seems to define a 200 OK with the MCUELocation should be answered but instead the description refers to 6.2.2.8 for a POST
"Upon receiving the HTTP POST request, the LMC shall: When the LMC receives that location request, then the LMC: 1) shall send a location report as specified in clause 6.2.2.8; and 2) shall reset the minimumReportInterval timer."
Additionally the need to add requestID to the request is only mentioned in 6.2.2.8.2 but not in 6.2.2.7.2.
#### 10.1.4 No explicit 200 OK to the SIP MESSAGE location reporting configuration request
Clause 13.3.21 in 3GPPT TS 24.379 defines the behaviour of a MCPTT Client receiving a location reporting configuration request from the participating (either triggered by the participating itself or initiated by an authorized client). Although 200 OK could be considered as the default behaviour upon reception of a SIP MESSAGE this is not explicitly indicated (while is in the originating authorized client -> participating step).
###### 10.1.5 Clarification of the authorization mechanism for location configuration request in step 7 c) i) in 13.2.2A
Step 7 c) seems to be extracted from 13.2.3.2 and might be updated indicating the authorization of the location reporting configuration, not location. It is not clear whether there is a single authorization for any location procedure and, additionally, clause 7.4 Location user configuration data document in TS 24.484 seems to be applicable to MCLoc (and not traditional location) only.
#### 10.1.6 RequestId in MCLoc Request - Publish sequence
Step 1 in clause 6.2.2.8.2 "LMC reports to LMS using LocationReportPublish" in 3GPPT TS 24.283, indicates that the MCUELocation datatype shall include "a reportID attribute if the report was triggered by a location request, set to the value of the requestID attribute in the received request". However, only reportId is described in the API definition in yaml document and requestID should be added.

## 10 Plugtests Observations to the FRMCS/MCX Standards As a result of the Plugtests event activities some issues in 3GPP Technical Specifications (TSs) and related standards were identified together with practical deployment problems that may demand some clarification or feedback from the related SDOs. We have classified those aspects into the following two categories: Observations to FRMCS/MCX Standards: Missing, erroneous or ambiguous definition of procedures in 3GPP's MCPTT TSs. - Technical constraints: Related to implementation issues, not covered by the standards, but which need to be faced by MCX vendors in most deployments. The reader should note that 3GPP Release 18 was considered for the fifth FRMCS Plugtests event. The $ 5^{th} $ FRMCS Plugtests event team wants to thank all the participants in the Plugtests for kindly sharing the following lessons learned. Specific actions towards pushing this feedback to relevant TSGs in 3GPP have already been started at the time of the release of this report. ### 10.1 Observations to FRMCS/MCX Standards #### 10.1.1 Lack of integrity/confidentiality protection in partner system for the migration deauthorized notification Test case 7.4.7 shows how the client in the partner system is capable of protecting the mcptt-id associated elements in the migration authorization request (that would be therefore hidden in the SIP/IMS Core of the partner system). However, there is no sibling behaviour for the primary system sending the deauthorized notification, since the SIP message (that could be in the clear in the path from the primary to the partner system) is simply forwarded between the participating and the migrated Client. #### 10.1.2 Late call entry and partner/primary affiliation depending on where the group is hosted Clause 10.16.2 in 3GPP TS 23.280 depicts a situation for late call entry when migrating but whether the "service continuity" like behaviour demands the user before and after migration to be affiliated to the same group in either the primary or the partner system is unclear. For example, Figure 10.16.2.2-1 seems to show that the late call entry is triggered by the server in the partner system (that would mean that the group is hosted there no matter steps 1 and 3 covering both primary/partner hosting options). #### 10.1.3 Unclear role of “MC Service FA Controlling Server” during Private call using functional alias towards a partner MC system Clause 10.16.3.3 in 3GPP TS 23.280 depicts a situation where the FA resolution procedure is forwarded from a -so called- FA controlling server in the primary system to the service FA controlling server in the partner. However Stage 3 (i.e. Section 11.1.1.3.1.1 in 3GPP TS 24.379) defines that the initial INVITE will be submitted to the PSI of the Controlling server associated with the originating user's MCPTT ID identity (step 6) (therefore not with the called FA) and from there, according to step 8a) in 11.1.1.4.2 will initiate the FA resolution mechanism (9A.2.2.2.8). Therefore, the FA resolution mechanism would be triggered by the Controlling in the primary system serving the calling MCPTT-ID and forwarded directly to the one owning the FA in the partner system (making step 4 unneeded).

#### 10.1.9 SSRC management in implicit floor/transmission request     MCPTT/MCVideo calls in controlling ⇔ non-controlling interface not defined
When a user initiates a call with implicit floor/transmission request, the controlling server tells the user which SSRC to use for every stream. However, in case of controlling/non-controlling scenarios, it is not defined who should define the SSRC, therefore clarification is requested.
#### 10.1.10 Missing MCData procedures for non-controlling
File distribution delivery/read notification, emergency alerts and upgrade/downgrade of emergency calls procedures are not defined for non-controlling node in 3GPP TS 24.282.
#### 10.1.11 CSK management for multi service (MCPTT/MCData/MCVideo) during service authorization
When service authentication is done during the registration (i.e. section 5.1.3.2.1 in 3GPP TS 33.180), the CSK is sent along the Access Token. Plugtest Participants request clarification regarding the situation where, assuming the CSK is different per service, how theoretically different CSKs per service should be included (i.e. should the MCS client send three different mikey-sakke payloads?).
#### 10.1.12 Format of UserID in KMS exchanges
In 3GPP TS 33.180 Release 16, the format of the UserID string was not specifically stated in Table D.3.3.2-1 (and actually the example in F.2.1 suggested an hexadecimal/OctetString). From Release 17+, the base64 encoding has been specified in both the table and F.2.1. Since that might eventually lead to backwards incompatibility between different releases KMS client and servers a Plugtests Participant suggests to add a "format" attribute to the XML tag (i.e. <UserID format="base64"> or <UserID format="OctetString">).
#### 10.1.13 KMS Key generation and test vectors
In 3GPP TS 33.180 F.2.1 for Release 19, UserID is replacing "ID" in RFC 6507/6508, as Tel-URI may not exist. However, the format to be provided for RFC 6507/6708 would be according to Plugtests participants a bit confusing. The RFC states "The format of Identifiers MUST be specified by each implementation." F.2.1 would according to some Plugtest Participant explain how to build the UserID, but not explicitly how to use it for RFC 6507/6708 (i.e. what is the
input of crypto functions or whether binary representation of the digest or the base64 encoded string of the digest -while the specified format of UserID and base on the fact that RFCs are taking URI's string as example-). Clear test vectors would greatly enhance validation of implementation and interoperability.
#### 10.1.14 Ambiguities in SSRCs to be used in different MCVideo transmission control messages
3GPP TS 24.581 Section 4.2.2 states that an MCVideo call uses 3 different and unique SSRC values. One for audio, one for video and another one for transmission control. It also states that the transmission participant is uniquely identified in the MCVideo call using the 'SSRC value'. This statement doesn't clarify which of the 3 SSRCs it is referring to. Even assuming this statement means the "SSRC used for Transmission Control" further issues may appear.

## Executive Summary
The capabilities of Mission Critical Push to Talk (MCPTT), Mission Critical Data (MCData) and Mission Critical Video (MCVideo) – together abbreviated as MCX services – were tested during the ninth MCX Plugtests from 24 $ ^{th} $ February to 28 $ ^{th} $ February 2025 at the The Center for Infrastructure Renewal (CIR) part of Texas A&M University System (TAMUS) in College Station, Texas, USA using 4G and 5G test networks. 174 test cases were executed between vendors, based on 3GPP Release 18.
The 9th ETSI MCX Plugtests have concluded with a success rate of 83% of the executed tests in the validation of 3GPP mission critical services vendor interoperability. More than 200 delegates participated during the  $ 9^{th} $ MCX Plugtests event on-site in College Station and off-site from their labs.

MCX采用符合3GPP标准的安全架构和机制，支持端到端加密，能够有效防止数据泄露、篡改和未经授权的访问。且兼容性强，能与其他符合该标准的系统在同样的安全机制下进行互操作。
- 1． **宽窄融合**
PoC作为独立的应用层服务，无法直接与TETRA、PDT、P25等窄带集群系统对接，若客户已有LMR投资，需额外采购专用网关且功能受限，通常仅能支持语音互通，数据和视频无法跨系统流转。
MCX在3GPP标准中明确定义了IWF互操作功能，可实现与LMR系统的标准化对接，帮助客户在保护既有投资的同时平滑向宽带演进。
- 1． **业务框架**
PoC的业务能力以语音对讲为核心，部分厂商扩展了定位、图文消息、视频通话等功能，但均为私有实现，无统一标准保障，视频和数据能力在质量、时延、可靠性方面取决于网络质量，适合简单工作协同场景。
MCX定义了三大标准化服务——MCPTT（关键任务一键通）、MCVideo（关键任务视频）、MCData（关键任务数据），每项服务均有明确的QoS指标、信令流程和优先级机制，可实现语音、视频、数据的一体化融合调度，支撑复杂业务场景。
- 1． **系统演进**
公网PoC：功能迭代依赖厂商自身规划，无统一技术演进路线。
MCX：依托3GPP标准持续迭代，R17已支持卫星接入（NTN），R18引入AI增强，未来可平滑升级至5G-A及6G，是行业未来十年关键通信的统一演进底座。
### 2.3 应用场景
| 场景              | 推荐方案        | 原因                                      |
|-----------------|-------------|-----------------------------------------|
| 警察、消防、急救指挥      | MCX         | 通信失败=生命损失                               |
| 铁路/地铁调度、港口/机场运营 | MCX         | 视频+数据是刚需，网络级保障  3GPP已定义铁路FRMCS标准替代GSM-R |

- 1、 **与LMR互通：**
1. 采用背靠背硬件网关，实现语音互通，MCX与网关直接通过SIP协议对接（主推，成本可控，能够快速部署系统，无知识产权风险）；
2. 支持基于3GPP标准的IWF方案，实现MCX与LMR互通。方案集成主流IWF产品厂家的设备，实现MCX与LMR系统的平滑融合。标准IWF方案需要协调LMR系统厂家的对接支持，以及不低的对接费用。目前，市场上IWF厂家少、产品少、价格高，同时需要LMR原厂协议、安全及数据对接支持，技术复杂、难度大，对接费用高，实施周期长。
## 4 终端
系统：小屏终端Android6及以上，大屏智能终端Android8及以上；
专载：UE需支持MCX DNN接入和访问。UE需支持标准QoS机制，支持MCX的专用承载，包括语音专用承载（5QI=65）、视频专用承载（5QI=67）、信令专用承载（5QI=69）和多媒体数据专用承载（5QI=70）。
IOS系统：iOS 版本当前暂未上线，后续会规划开发；现阶段我们重点优化系统稳定性、完善产品功能。

PMR/LMR运行在独立窄带专网，与民用宽带完全隔离，无线域内资源自主可控。
在专用或混合网络部署下，MCX通过3GPP标准化的QoS策略和优先级抢占机制，可在网络拥塞时保障关键会话不中断。纯公网部署时，效果取决于运营商的优先级策略配置。OTT部署则不具备该特性。
- 1． **互操作性**
PMR/LMR跨厂商、跨标准（如TETRA与P25之间）的互通需要专用网关，基本仅限语音业务。
MCX基于3GPP全球统一标准，支持多厂商互通。通过IWF（Interworking Function，互操作功能）可与现有PMR/LMR系统无缝互联，实现平滑过渡。
- 1． **系统过渡路径**
大多数行业的宽带升级都是渐进式落地。多数机构会保留原有PMR/LMR系统保障关键语音不间断，同时引入MCX关键任务通信，承载宽带协同业务、拓展广域覆盖。
依托标准化互通网关等宽窄融合互通方案，各单位可在过渡期实现两套系统并行调度，无需一次性关停原有系统、中断业务。
- 1． **安全性**
PMR/LMR安全主要依赖空口加密和物理网络隔离，安全模型相对封闭。
MCX采用符合3GPP标准的安全架构和机制，支持端到端加密，能够有效防止数据泄露、篡改和未经授权的访问。且兼容性强，能与其他符合该标准的系统在同样的安全机制下进行互操作。
- 1． **成本与演进**
PMR/LMR采用高CAPEX（资本支出）自建模式，但生命周期长（10-15年）。设备供应商正在逐步减少对传统技术的支持，新建项目趋于萎缩。
MCX采用低CAPEX、灵活OPEX模式，支持软件持续迭代。3GPP标准持续演进，可融入AI、6G等前沿技术。
### 1.3 应用场景

| 终端   | 夜视                   | 在黑暗的情况下，可自动切换到夜视模式                                                                                                    | 行业通用     |
| 终端   | 人脸识别                 | 可在本地做人脸算法，识别可疑人物，并报警                                                                                                  | 行业通用     |
| 终端   | 广角                   | 可大广角进行录制，主要为了人脸识别。                                                                                                    | 行业通用     |
| 终端   | 红外                   | 在救援环境下，进行红外录入                                                                                                         | 行业通用     |
| 需产研评估确认   |
|-----------|
|  PTT/MCSTARS   | 调度台声音提醒            | 终端视频直播时，通知调度员正在录制/直播视频（用户开始录制后需要有一个声音提醒调度员，这个用户开始录制了），以便调度员能够轻松查看和监听现场情况                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 未实现   |

**MCX与LMR、PoC对比说明V1.0**
## 1 MCX关键任务通信系统 VS LMR窄带集群通信系统
### 1.1 系统概述
- **PMR( Professional Mobile Radio，专业移动无线电)/ LMR（Land Mobile Radio，陆地移动无线电）**
PMR/LMR是数十年来公共安全、应急指挥和关键行业的通信基石，依托专属窄带频谱自建基站组网，以低时延对讲语音为核心，部分仅支持 GPS、短报文等低速数据，具备本地高可靠、自主可控、极端环境稳定通信优势，但带宽不足无法承载视频、大流量数据。
- **MCX（Mission Critical Services，关键任务通信系统）**
MCX是由3GPP标准化的宽带关键任务通信框架，基于LTE/5G网络，包含三大核心服务：MCPTT（关键任务一键通）、MCVideo（关键任务视频）和MCData（关键任务数据）。它标志着宽带技术被正式规范以满足关键任务通信的严苛要求。MCX主打高可靠、强安全、可演进、可宽窄融合，支持跨系统、跨区域、跨国互联互通，支持大规模组网部署，适配公共安全、应急救援、轨道交通、能源电网等关键任务场景。
### 1.2 核心差异对比
- 1． **技术基础**
PMR/LMR经历了从模拟集群到数字集群的技术演进，模拟时代主要包括MPT-1327、LTR等标准；数字时代则主要包括TETRA（欧洲ETSI制定的高端集群标准）、DMR（ETSI制定的全球开放数字无线电标准，含集群/常规模式）、P25（北美TIA制定的公共安全标准）、PDT（中国公安部制定的警用数字集群标准）等专有窄带技术。这些标准由各自的标准化组织或厂商联盟独立制定，技术体系相对独立，跨制式互通需专用网关设备，跨厂商设备的兼容性也存在一定挑战。
MCX基于3GPP制定的LTE/5G开放标准，是全球移动通信产业统一的技术框架，涵盖MCPTT（关键任务一键通）、MCVideo（关键任务视频）和MCData（关键任务数据）三大核心服务。其技术开放性使得不同厂商的设备能够基于统一标准实现互联互通，大幅降低了跨系统、跨区域的集成难度。MCX支持持续的功能迭代和演进，能够随3GPP标准版本更新不断引入新能力，技术生命周期更具弹性。

agent_answer:
MCX 系统间以及与异系统（LMR 类窄带系统）的对接方式不同，知识库中记载如下：

## 一、MCX 系统间互通（MCX—MCX）

网络侧支持**两种互通模式**，实现跨系统通信和数据交换：

1. **标准接口互通**：当多个 MCX 系统均在**同一运营商 5G 网络内**时，通过标准接口实现互通；
2. **MC 网关服务器互通**：当 MCX 系统分布在**多个运营商 5G 网络内**时，通过 MC 网关服务器实现互通。MC 网关服务器位于每个网络的边缘，可确保进入每个网络的通信安全性并实现拓扑隐藏，使各网络互不了解对方内部细节，保障互通下的安全隔离。

图 5 MCX 系统间互联互通架构：

![MCX 系统间互联互通架构](imgs/img_in_image_box_162_210_944_590.jpg)

## 二、与异系统（LMR 窄带系统）互通

MCX 系统通过支持 **IWF（Interworking Function，互通功能）网关互联**，实现与 LMR 系统（如 P25、TETRA、PDT 等窄带集群系统）的互联互通。其中：

- IWF 网关与 LMR 系统的接口需适配 LMR 不同的技术体制；
- 互联互通应实现语音单呼、语音组呼、紧急呼叫、短消息等关键业务，并明确语音编解码方案、编号规则及安全标准，确保两系统间业务的一致性、可靠性和安全性；
- 针对我国 PDT 系统，由于两系统在集群业务特性、协议标准及功能实现上存在差异，实际互通中可能需要对架构进行优化，并对接口进行增强和适配（包括语音组呼、单呼、优先级处理、紧急呼叫等关键功能的协调），以及针对信令协议、数据传输和安全机制进行调整。

图 6 MCX 系统与 LMR 系统互通架构：

![MCX 系统与 LMR 系统互通架构](imgs/img_in_image_box_287_1143_804_1462.jpg)

## 补充

产品白皮书另记载：MCX 系统、终端之间采用 **SIP 标准协议**，接口互通互联、兼容；系统基于 **3GPP R18 协议标准**并持续演进，保证与核心网和其他 MCX 系统互通互联。产品网元中亦包含 **MCIWF（Mission Critical InterWorking Function Gateway）**，提供系统间互通网关功能（例如与 LMR 窄带系统互通）。

##### 2.2.2.4 跨域融合 ###### 2.2.2.4.1 MCX 系统间互通 当前很多关键任务场景涉及多个 MCX 系统共存，比如跨区域应急救援、多部门联动任务等，这些独立的 MCX 系统若无法互通，会形成“通信孤岛”，导致语音组呼、定位数据、应急指令等关键信息无法传递，不同的应急响应机构无法即时共享信息和协调行动，直接阻碍协作效率，甚至延误救援、调度等关键任务。 针对上述痛点问题，网络侧需要支持接口互通和与 MC 网关服务器互通两种模式，如图 5 所示，进而实现跨系统通信和数据交换的能力。当多个 MCX 系统均在同一运营商 5G 网络内，可以通过标准接口互通。当 MCX 系统分布在多个运营商 5G 网络内，通过 MC 网关服务器实现互通。MC 网关服务器位于每个网络的边缘，确保进入每个网络的通信安全性并实现拓扑隐藏，使得各网络互相不了解对方的内部细节，保障互通下的安全隔离。
图 5 MCX 系统间互联互通架构
###### 2.2.2.4.2 异构系统互通 在 MCX 技术现世前，LMR 已经历了较长的发展历程，包含了从早期简单的模拟通信系统到窄带数字通信系统多种类型，且多国家为了保障公共安全已大面积部署窄带集群系统，比如 P25 系统、TETRA 系统、PDT 系统等。其中，PDT 是我国专门为满足公共安全、应急通信和行业专网的高效、可靠通信需求而设计的数字无线通信系统，已实现全国覆盖。因此，MCX 除了同系统间互通，宽窄融合互通能力也是必选项。

为满足上述需求，MCX 通信系统应支持 IWF（Interworking Function，互通功能）网关互联，进而实现 MCX 系统与 LMR 系统互联互通，如图 6 所示。其中，IWF 网关与 LMR 系统接口需适配 LMR 不同的技术体制。互联互通应实现语音单呼、语音组呼、紧急呼叫、短消息等关键业务，同时应明确语音编解码方案、编号规则及安全标准，确保两系统间的业务一致性、可靠性和安全性。
图 6 MCX 系统与 LMR 系统互通架构
MCX 系统与我国 PDT 系统在集群业务特性、协议标准以及功能实现上都存在一定差异，为了确保用户能够在两种系统之间获得一致且流畅的业务体验，实际的互通过程中可能需要对架构进行优化，并对接口进行增强和适配，包括对语音组呼、单呼、优先级处理、紧急呼叫等关键功能的协调，确保不同系统间的互操作性。同时，可能还需要针对信令协议、数据传输和安全机制等方面进行调整，以实现跨系统的无缝集成和业务一致性。 #### 2.2.3 “2”类通信模式 ##### 2.2.3.1 在网呼叫 在关键任务场景中，常面临网络覆盖正常的常规作业情境，比如日常跨部门调度、大型活动安保协同等，这类场景主要对单呼、组呼、MBS等功能存在强烈需求，指挥者通过单呼能够向特定人员传递精准指令，团队能够借助组呼功能同步战术细节，并通过MBS向多终端高效下发全局部署信息，实现各参与方信息同步、行动协调，显著提高常规关键任务的处置效率。 基于上述场景需求，为了提高 MCX 业务的通信可靠性，当有 5G 网络覆盖时，MCX 通信系统应支持单呼、MBS 组播广播功能。
